profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, traded on public markets under the ticker NVDA. Its most recently reported annual revenue was $215,938,000,000, filed on a 10-K covering the period ending January 25, 2026. The company develops hardware and software for artificial intelligence, data science, and related workloads.

NVIDIA's Nemotron is described on its site as a family of multimodal, open AI models built for agentic reasoning tasks including graduate-level science, advanced mathematics, visual understanding, speech recognition, text-to-speech, neural machine translation, and retrieval-augmented generation. The site says Nemotron models are available under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without attribution, and that NVIDIA publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques openly. Specific variants mentioned include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, positioned for faster specialized task completion, and NeMo Switchyard, described as a routing layer that directs workflow steps to appropriate models. The site also names Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, as a spokesperson for the project. NVIDIA NIM, tracked separately as an inference microservice product, is the deployment vehicle for Nemotron models in enterprise settings and requires an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for that use; models and NIM microservices can be accessed at build.nvidia.com.

The held facts note no litigation or MCP server registry presence for NVIDIA. The company's CIK with the SEC is 0001045810.
